class_name: 進行-慣習-コトニナッテイル類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Names a standing arrangement: a schedule, rule or agreement that holds independently of the speaker's will (靴を脱ぐことになっている), which makes it the usual way to state workplace and school rules. Contrast ことにしている, which reports the speaker's own resolve; Japanese often prefers ことになっている even for decisions the speaker did make, to keep the statement impersonal.

examples.ruby: 面接[めんせつ]の結果[けっか]は来週[らいしゅう]伝[つた]えることになっている。
examples.english: The interview results are due to be given out next week.

examples.ruby: この部屋[へや]では靴[くつ]を脱[ぬ]ぐことになってる。
examples.english: You're supposed to take your shoes off in this room.

examples.ruby: 部活[ぶかつ]の後[あと]の片付[かたづ]けは一年生[いちねんせい]がすることになっています。
examples.english: The first-years are the ones supposed to clean up after club practice.
